Hi Daniel / Trinity procurement team,

Thanks for taking this initial call last week. SummitCare's program team asked us to put together a concise feasibility check for a combined HIPAA (BAA) + GLBA addendum for the product integration you're evaluating with Redwood. High-level asks from SummitCare:
- Confirm whether we can contractually support a combined BAA + GLBA addendum (single rider) or if separate instruments are required.
- Confirm data residency gating (US-only, restricted to specific regions / AZs) and whether we can guarantee no EU transfers for this account.
- Provide our current subprocessor list and an option for customer approval gating / notification cadence.
- Confirm what footprint (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) is required to meet GLBA+BAA obligations and any timeline/cost delta.

Attached is a short one-pager that outlines our typical approach for regulated addenda and a draft DPA snapshot. Can you share your vendor packet / security questionnaire so our legal + security teams can align?

Proposed next step: a 30-min follow-up technical session w/ SummitCare security + Redwood infra + legal. Are you available next Tue or Wed (09:00-13:00 PT)?

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Manager, Regulated Accounts
Redwood Inference

Hi Priya,

Appreciate the summary. We typically prefer a single consolidated rider if the vendor can meet both GLBA and HIPAA controls without caveats; otherwise we accept a combined set of obligations with clear scoping.

I've attached SummitCare's vendor security packet and a short procurement checklist — that'll give you the clauses we care most about (data residency, encryption-at-rest, KMS controls, subprocessor approval and notification windows, breach reporting timelines).

Quick answers to unblock scheduling: we want US-only residency (primary + DR in US regions), customer approval required for any subprocessor that accesses PHI or financial data, and proof of SOC2 + BAA.

We can do Tue 2027-08-24 at 10:00 PT for the technical session. Please include your infra/security and legal.

Regards,
Daniel Carter
Sr. Information Security Manager, SummitCare Health

Thanks for the context. Short answers up-front: yes — feasible with guardrails. Detailed notes below.

1) Combined rider: Legal can draft a single rider that references both HIPAA (BAA obligations) and GLBA-specific clauses (nonpublic personal information, financial data handling). The rider should:
   - Clearly scope PHI vs FFI (financial) by data elements and API endpoints.
   - Include segregation and access controls for PHI processing.

2) Residency / transfers:
   - Hosted (shared multitenant) does not guarantee strict AZ-level residency or process-level isolation; we can provide region restrictions but cannot promise dedicated physical isolation.
   - Recommended path: Redwood Dedicated (reserved pools) or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) to satisfy US-only residency + contractual no-EU-transfer guarantees.
   - We can offer contractual commitments for data-at-rest and in-transit encryption; however, cross-border backups and analytics (if used) must be disabled / contractually restricted.

3) Subprocessors and gating:
   - Current subprocessors that commonly touch regulated data: AWS (S3, EC2), Google Cloud KMS (if used), Sentry (errors), Segment (if customer enables). See attached subprocessor_matrix.csv (redacted).
   - We can implement explicit approval for any subprocessor that will access PHI or FFI. The workflow: Redwood provides 30 days notice + customer may request mitigation or propose alternatives; if approvals are withheld, we route to Dedicated/Private deployment as a fallback.

4) DPA redlines:
   - Add explicit KMS key custody language (customer-managed keys for PHI).
   - Add a 30-day subprocessor approval window and a clause enabling a migration to Dedicated within 60 days if new subprocessors cannot be approved.
   - Incident response: align to 72-hour initial notification for breaches impacting PHI/FFI.

I'll join the 8/24 call from infra/security. For the session, we should bring: one product engineer (deployment architecture), one infra/security engineer (subprocessor matrix + KMS options), and legal (Laura) for contractual scope.

Attaching the redacted subprocessor matrix and a short implementation checklist.

—Rishi

Daniel — thanks for the packet and for confirming the 8/24 slot. Quick summary and proposed next steps from Redwood's side so we're all aligned before the call: 

Summary: 
- Redwood confirms a single consolidated rider is viable; we will propose DPA language that maps BAA obligations to the GLBA scoping items.
- For strict US-only residency and contractual no-EU-transfer guarantees, we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) or Private (VPC) depending on your tolerance for ops ownership and timeline.
- We can offer an explicit subprocessor approval workflow (30-day notice + approval window); if a required subprocessor cannot be approved, we will migrate the workload to Dedicated/Private within 60 days per the rider.

Action items: 
1) Redwood to send a prioritized redline (legal) within 3 business days after the 8/24 call — link to draft DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.example.com/ABC-Redwood-SummitCare
2) Security/Infra (Redwood) to share a single-page KMS options brief (customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed) and the redacted subprocessor matrix — attached.
3) Schedule a technical follow-up if Trinity needs additional procurement inputs (we can loop them into the 8/24 notes).

If this looks good, we'll proceed to circulate the rider redline and schedule a deep-dive architecture session the week of 8/30.

Best,
